invariant: Only aircraft or components satisfying every supported applicability predicate may receive released matches or due state.
summary: Serial, equipment, expression, and general applicability predicates are persisted but not evaluated by matching.
impact: Known non-applicable aircraft can receive actionable AD matches and due state.
requiredClosure: Evaluate supported predicates and force adjudication for every unknown or unimplemented predicate; add negative range, exclusion, equipment, and expression tests.
closureEvidence: Tri-state serial/equipment/expression/condition evaluation now fails unsupported predicates to adjudication; negative applicability tests pass in the 70-test focused AD suite.

invariant: Every release and derived-state consumer is bound to the exact evidence-valid human-signed extraction.
summary: Catalog and matching accept approved extraction status without exact decided-review identity and output equality.
impact: Unsigned or mutated extraction data can be consumed under another extraction's valid evidence.
requiredClosure: Centralize a released-signed-extraction boundary and use it for catalog, matching, coverage, rematerialization, and exact match reads.
closureEvidence: backend/app/services/ad_release.py centralizes exact signed-extraction verification and reconciles catalog, matching, coverage, due-state, and rematerialization consumers; mutation regressions pass.

invariant: Every current signed v3 obligation is replayed and exposed independently of compatibility summaries.
summary: Legacy complianceIntervals controls recurrence and only one requirement/due state is attached to a match.
impact: Required obligations can disappear from actionable compliance state.
requiredClosure: Drive replay from all current signed requirements and model/expose due state per obligation/component.
closureEvidence: Matching and recurrence now enumerate exact extraction/applicability requirements per component and expose independent due states; multi-group and multi-component regressions pass.

invariant: Migrations never amend signed regulatory meaning and rollback never silently destroys unrepresentable v3 state.
summary: Migration 0023 adds empty AMOC meaning to signed JSON and earlier downgrades destroy v3 semantics.
impact: Migration can forge human decision meaning or erase regulatory evidence.
requiredClosure: Reopen missing-envelope reviews with attributed audit evidence and implement an explicit guarded irreversible recovery contract or lossless export.
closureEvidence: Migration 0024 conservatively reopens and snapshots the full ambiguous v3 cohort, uses SHA-256 audit hashes, is idempotent, and guards downgrade before destructive DDL; PostgreSQL verifier reports 11 passed out of 11.

invariant: Component due state uses component-bound measurements unless an explicit reviewed equivalence proves another source valid.
summary: Component recurrence silently falls back to aircraft-level time state.
impact: Component intervals can be calculated from unrelated aircraft time and become actionable.
requiredClosure: Return unknown without component-bound time or an explicit reviewed equivalence; add mismatched-time tests.
closureEvidence: Component recurrence no longer falls back to unrelated aircraft time; missing component-bound measurement returns unknown/adjudication and focused negative tests pass.

invariant: Correction immediately revokes every derived regulatory row and reader until reapproval.
summary: Correction leaves applicability, requirements, AMOCs, due states, and coverage current.
impact: Stale regulatory state remains observable after revocation.
requiredClosure: Supersede or quarantine all derived rows and test every reader before reapproval.
closureEvidence: The correction transaction supersedes applicability, requirements, and AMOCs; clears due state and matches; quarantines coverage; reopens review; snapshots the decision; and excludes release. Committed PostgreSQL verifier reports 12 passed out of 12.

invariant: Each human decision is serialized, immutable, and fully actor/output attributed.
summary: Concurrent pending decisions can overwrite reviewer identity and signed output.
impact: Last writer wins and the first decision is not preserved as an immutable record.
requiredClosure: Lock or compare-and-set the transition, append immutable decision history, and add concurrency tests.
closureEvidence: Review decisions use a PostgreSQL row lock and append immutable decision history; the committed concurrency verifier reports 7 passed out of 7.

invariant: Every safety-bearing structured value is mechanically bound to cited source text or remains adjudication-blocked.
summary: Real citations can support unrelated manufacturer, model, serial, equipment, condition, and AMOC fields.
impact: Fabricated structured applicability can be approved behind genuine but unrelated text.
requiredClosure: Bind every critical field to exact citation text or force adjudication; add mismatch tests.
closureEvidence: Approval validates cited manufacturer/model identity, product role, serial/model scope, equipment, conditions, timing anchors, combination logic, dates, actions, and AMOC semantics; mismatch regressions pass in the focused AD suite.

invariant: Approval and release evidence identity matches the retained bytes reviewers can open.
summary: Cached pages trust mutable database hashes and retained bytes are not rehashed at approval/release.
impact: Review can validate cached text while the opened retained object contains different bytes.
requiredClosure: Rehash retained bytes or bind immutable object versions at approval/release and test storage mutation.
closureEvidence: Approval/release rehash exact retained bytes, re-derive cached page text, require exact document/page coverage and current extraction input hash, and the content endpoint serves that same verified buffer; mutation/omission/correction tests pass.

invariant: Calibration exercises the v3 failure modes claimed by the design.
summary: The five calibration files are requirement-only drafts rather than complete v3 packets.
impact: Calibration cannot prove group, serial, equipment, AMOC, correction, or exact-release behavior.
requiredClosure: Produce complete cited v3 packets and expected positive/negative adjudication outcomes.
disposition: Human calibration intentionally follows the completed Claude and adversarial implementation gates; incomplete records remain pending and cannot publish or drive released matching.
revisitCondition: Before broader AD release, complete and human-review all five cited v3 packets with expected positive and negative aircraft/component outcomes.

invariant: Each permitted migration downgrade reconstructs its exact parent schema or fails before DDL.
summary: Migration 0022 downgrade restores the legacy four-column constraint instead of 0021's five-column constraint.
impact: A database labeled 0021 can have an incompatible schema and fail later upgrades or group persistence.
requiredClosure: Restore the five-column constraint for 0022 to 0021, keep four columns only for 0021 to 0020, preflight before DDL, and test schema fidelity and atomic failure.
closureEvidence: Migration downgrades preflight before DDL and restore the exact parent constraint shape; the isolated PostgreSQL upgrade/downgrade verifier reports 11 passed out of 11.

invariant: Every decision ambiguously amended by migration 0023 is conservatively identified, audited, and reopened.
summary: The prior migration did not record touched IDs and the proposed repair did not define a deterministic cohort.
impact: Forged empty-AMOC meaning can remain approved or legitimate reviewed emptiness can be silently rewritten.
requiredClosure: Define a conservative cohort, preserve hashes/output and reason, reopen every ambiguous decision, and test reruns, partial state, legitimate empty lists, and zero surviving ambiguous approvals.
closureEvidence: Migration 0024 snapshots null, empty, nonempty, partial, and terminal decision states, reopens the complete absent-origin cohort with an explicit repair actor, preserves legitimate payloads, and proves rerun idempotency in PostgreSQL.

invariant: Every applicability and downstream row is immutably bound to the exact signed extraction that authored it.
summary: Applicability identity lacks source extraction and later extractions can overwrite rows under an earlier signature.
impact: Coverage and matching cannot prove which signed extraction authored current applicability.
requiredClosure: Add source-extraction or materialization-generation identity, quarantine ambiguous legacy rows, join every consumer through exact identity, and add two-extraction tests.
closureEvidence: Applicability rows now carry source_extraction_id, v3 uniqueness includes it, legacy ambiguous rows are superseded, and released readers reconcile relational rows to the exact signed JSON; cross-extraction mutation tests pass.

invariant: Every published field is supported by an exact citation from the target AD section; neighboring regulatory text is never citation-eligible.
summary: Issue bounding previously admitted the remaining document when a target rule footer was missing.
impact: A neighboring rule could have supplied wording for a misattributed structured value.
requiredClosure: Fail closed when no trustworthy target footer exists and cover missing, OCR-corrupted, and later-rule footer cases.
closureEvidence: bounded_issue_pages now returns no evidence without the target footer and rejects any later document boundary before a valid footer, including a non-Part-39 neighbor; 8 passed out of 8 targeted bounding tests and 71 passed out of 71 focused AD tests.

invariant: Every administrative mutation is actor-attributed and its authentication boundary is explicit.
summary: Direct-database scripts cannot cryptographically prove that a caller-supplied actor ID is the shell operator.
impact: A privileged shell operator could attribute a staged proposal or correction to another active platform administrator.
requiredClosure: Either use session authentication or explicitly accept the direct-database trust tier and record an actor for every mutation.
disposition: Accepted for local privileged operations: shell and database access are the authentication boundary. Both scripts now require and validate an active platform-admin actor and persist that identity; normal human decisions remain restricted to authenticated HTTP.
revisitCondition: Before exposing either script through a remote job runner or delegating shell/database access beyond trusted operators, replace caller-supplied attribution with a signed operator/session identity.

invariant: Calibration exercises complete v3 group, serial, equipment, AMOC, correction, and negative adjudication cases.
summary: The five human calibration records remain requirement-only drafts rather than complete reviewed v3 packets.
impact: The real-document calibration set cannot yet serve as end-to-end regression evidence.
requiredClosure: Complete the five records through the authenticated admin GUI with positive and negative expected outcomes.
disposition: Deferred to the next human-review loop as requested; all incomplete records remain pending/source-quarantined and cannot publish.
revisitCondition: Complete before any broader AD catalog release or reliance on the five-record set as calibration evidence.

invariant: Review prose accurately identifies the current database head and reviewed migration scope.
summary: The decision prose named migration 0023 even though 0024 is the current implementation head.
impact: A reviewer could under-scope the corrective materialization migration.
requiredClosure: Name migration 0024, its purpose, and the current head in the decision packet.
closureEvidence: decision.md and GOAL_TASKS.md now identify 20260823_0024 as head and include it in migration scope; the closure packet will be regenerated from current files.
